text.tspan: flags and the string DSL do the same work — use whichever reads better
-d runs the gradient down the lines instead of across them
-s picks the interpolation space, -b paints the background
grfti "blue, yellow" -s rgb "rgb, the way most tools do it"
grfti "blue, yellow" -s oklab "oklab, the way grfti does it"
grfti sunset -b " painted behind the text "
every flag has a DSL equivalent, so a config file and a shell call agree
